_note: Inputs to the compute-budget calculation, separated by whether they were
MEASURED or ASSUMED. Every assumption carries `measured: false` so that a
forecast built on guesses cannot be mistaken for one built on evidence.
Refresh the measured block by running a real generation and reading the

fx.note: paise per dollar. A rate baked into code is a cost model that drifts.

note: Measured at ONE question per call, which is the pessimistic case: the
prompt is not amortised across a batch. A 10-question batch would spend
far fewer input tokens per question. Budgeting on the pessimistic figure
Production acceptance has NOT been measured. The adversarial battery
measured the validator's detection rate on planted defects, which is a
different quantity. 80 is a placeholder and is flagged as one.
Regenerations are deliberately NOT a separate multiplier here: a
regenerated question is a PRODUCED question, already counted by this
ratio. Adding both would double-count the same work.
Free questions come out of the same provider credit as paid ones and
have no revenue line of their own. Ignoring them is the single most
common way a free tier bankrupts the product that offers it.
